label: rem:hamilton-jacobi-phase
title: Hamilton--Jacobi equation for the phase and classical trajectories
html:
The Madelung decomposition \psi = \sqrt{\rho}\exp(JS/\hbar_q) separates the Schrödinger equation into continuity (for \rho) and quantum Euler (for v = \nabla_A S) equations. The equation for the phase S itself — the quantum Hamilton--Jacobi equation — forms the other face of the Madelung picture, linking the brane fluid directly to classical mechanics.

The q-deformed Hamilton--Jacobi equation. Substituting \psi into the q-deformed Schrödinger equation and isolating the real part yields

  \partial_t S
  + 
  \frac{1}{2}\lVert\nabla_A S\rVert^2
  +  V
  +  Q_q
  =  0,

where V is the external potential (curvature of the \mathrm{SU}(2) connection) and Q_q = -(\hbar_q^2/2)\Delta_q\sqrt{\rho}/\sqrt{\rho} is the quantum pressure. This constitutes the Hamilton--Jacobi equation for a classical particle in the potential V + Q_q. The term Q_q completely absorbs the quantum correction.

Classical trajectories. The characteristics of the Hamilton--Jacobi equation define the classical trajectories

  \dot{x} = \nabla_A S(x, t),
  \qquad
  \dot{p} = -\nabla_A(V + Q_q).

These correspond precisely to the geodesics of the acoustic metric g_{\mathrm{ac}} once Q_q acts as an effective potential. The velocity field v = \nabla_A S is therefore simultaneously:

  1. the fluid velocity of the Madelung fluid,
  2. the momentum field of the Hamilton--Jacobi flow,
  3. the tangent vector to the acoustic geodesics.

This triple equivalence explains why geodesic vortices — critical points of the q-energy functional — also trace classical particle trajectories.

WKB hierarchy and the q-expansion. Expanding S = S_0 + \hbar_qS_1 + \hbar_q^2S_2 + \cdots produces a functional hierarchy:

  • O(1): Eikonal equation. \partial_t S_0 + \frac{1}{2}\lVert\nabla_A S_0\rVert^2 + V = 0. This gives the classical Hamilton--Jacobi equation without quantum corrections. Its characteristics trace the classical geodesics of the GR substrate geometry.
  • O(\hbar_q): Transport equation. \partial_t S_1 + \nabla_A S_0 \cdot \nabla_A S_1 = -\frac{1}{2}\Delta_q S_0. This governs amplitude modulation along classical rays and originates the algebraic filter: the q-Laplacian \Delta_q selects which modes propagate.
  • O(\hbar_q^2): Quantum pressure. S_2 introduces the quantum pressure Q_q. Trajectories at this order deviate from classical geodesics and spiral into vortex filaments, marking the onset of fermionic behaviour.

Caustics and vortex nucleation. The Hamilton--Jacobi solution S naturally develops caustics — loci where \nabla_A^2 S diverges and \rho \to \infty. In classical optics, these act as focal points; in the brane fluid, they act as vortex nucleation sites. At a caustic, the eikonal approximation fails and the full q-Schrödinger equation takes over. The resolution replaces the caustic with a vortex filament carrying quantised circulation [j]_q[j+1]_q, managing the transition from wave optics to particle physics.

Connection to the discrete spectrum. The Hamilton--Jacobi phase S is single-valued modulo 2\pi\hbar_q. The phase winding around a vortex filament \varrho accrues

  \oint_\varrho \nabla_A S \cdot dl
  = 
  2\pi\hbar_qn,
  \qquad n \in \mathbb{Z},

enforcing the Bohr--Sommerfeld quantisation condition. The q-deformation upgrades the integer n to the spin label j under \mathrm{SU}_q(2) representation theory: permitted phase windings measure 2\pi\hbar_q[j]_q rather than 2\pi\hbar_qn. This grounds the Hamilton--Jacobi picture in the discrete vortex spectrum and completes the correspondence between wave mechanics, fluid dynamics, and knot particles.
